speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, such as whether it's flat, raised, or has blisters? Also, when did the rash first appear relative to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash resemble "slapped cheeks," and have you noticed any lace-like or net-like patterns on her arms and legs? Additionally, has she experienced any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "slapped cheek" appearance and the lace-like pattern on your arms and legs are classic signs of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. Given your age and symptom timeline, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
